div.head: Rect 1
div.ab: [1] Ðegenes lagu. Ðegenlagu is, þæt he sy his bocrihtes wyrðe 7 þæt he ðreo ðinc of his lande do: fyrdfæreld 7 burhbote 7 brycgeweorc.
De lege taini. Taini lex est, ut sit dignus rectitudine testamenti sui et ut tria faciat pro terra sua, scilicet expeditionem, burhbotam et brugbotam.
ĐEGENES LAGV . ĐEGEN LAGV IS þæt he sy his boc rihtes wyr|ðe . 7 þæt he ðreo ðinc of his lande do fyrd|færeld . 7 burhbote 7 brycgeweorc .
Ðegenlagu is þæt he sy his bocrihtes wyrðe, and þæt he ðreo ðinc of his lande do: fyrdfæreld and burhbote and brycgeweorc.

The law of the thegn The law of the thegn is that he should be worthy of his book-rights, and that from his land he [must] do three things: levy a company, and be liable for the building and repair of town walls, and build bridges.
The thane’s duty is to fulfill the obligations of his charter, and do three things with his estate: raise a militia, oversee the upkeep of the buildings and walls, and repair the bridges.

Recht und Pflicht des Thegn [als Herrn des Grossguts]. Thegnrecht und -pflicht ist, dass er seines Urkundenrechtes [d. h. des Vorrechtes, welches ihm der König verbrieft hat in der Urkunde, kraft welcher er ihm das Gut bestätigte oder verlieh] geniesse und von seinem Lande drei Dinge [dem Staate] leiste: Landwehr-Heerfahrt und Festungsherstellung und Brückenwerk [Strassenbau].

The right and duty of the thegn [as lord of a great estate]. The thegn's law is that he be entitled to his charter-right [i.e. the privilege the king granted him by the charter by which he confirmed or granted him the estate] and that he render three things [to the state] from his land: service in the army, repair of fortifications, and bridge-work [road-building].

note.label: recalls
note.quote: the stress in Rect. 1 on a thegn's triple duty … recalls the decree drafted by Wulfstan at Enham, VI Atr 32:3

div.note: Liebermann's text is from B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 96, after Dunsæte, c. 1125, then belonging to St Paul's, London), the same manuscript as the modern edition. The headings are in red; some show Middle English forms (16 f.) and, where the Quadripartitus lacks them, are perhaps not archetypal and probably none are original. The Quadripartitus has a heading ‘De dignitate hominum (Rectitudines singularum personarum)’; Liebermann's German heading is ‘Gerechtsame der Leute [des Edelguts]’. Liebermann thinks the author a clerically trained reeve of a thegn's estate chartered by the king, writing late West Saxon, after 960 and before 1066, perhaps after 1017; Gerefa appears as its continuation. Liebermann compares VI Atr 26.1.
Manuscripts: B = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 383, fols. 63v–66v.
